newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following the suspension of Australis Media Ltd shares on the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday because of a failure to inform the market of its future, the company has undergone a revamp, with Foxtel partners News Corp and Telstra taking a 65 per cent hareholding under a plan expected to be approved today. Page 1.

The Australian Securities Commission has dealt Australia's leading independent stockbroker JB Were & Son only a minor punishment after Were admitted it had breached the Corporations Law in its handling of the sale of New Corporation's 40 per cent stake in PMP Communications. Page 37.

Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation has boosted its funds to around A$4.8 billion following the sale of Heritage Media's broadcast arm in the United States. News Corporation sold Heritage's six television stations and 24 radio stations to United States brodcast group Sinclair Broadcasting for US$630 million. Page 37.

In a move that places pressure on the 650-store Amcal Chemists co-operative to meets its members' demands for improved franchise services, FH Faulding & Co Ltd is to rationalise its 3,000 client chemists into four key banner groups, and will introduce a 20-store franchise based on successful United States chain The Medicine Shoppe. Page 38.

A report by Bankers Trust has told shareholders in troubled food ingredients group Burns Philp & Co Ltd to consider protecting themselves against a multi-million dollar payout by investing in Meridian Investment Group. The recommendation comes as litigaton between the former Estate Mortgage Group, its trustees and Burns Philp resumed this week. Page 39.

Steel production in BHP Co Ltd troubled steel division fell by 5 per cent in June, with the Newcastle steelworks losing a third of its production, and the Whyalla works reporting a 20 per cent drop in output. BHP's petroleum and copper divisions also reported poor figures, while the minerals division reported steady output for iron ore and coal. Page 41.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Stock Exchange yesterday suspended the trading of shares in Australis Media to ensure there was no uninformed trading overnight. The suspension came as Australis shares closed 5.5 per cent higher at 20 cents following speculation over a posible merger with cable TV operator Foxtel. Page 25.

As the coal industry is suffers from the dispute between Rio Tinto and unions, BHP Coal's human resources general manager, Julia Fellows, has reassured union delegates at a meeting on Wednesday that it remains committed to its controversial six-year frameork agreement with the Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union. Page 25.

Moonstone Diamond Corp NL will pay A$6.3 million for the Saxendrift mine near the Orange River in South Africa. As Moonstone's marine diamond mining is yet to reach expected levels, the latest purchase is seen as a good deal that will target high-value gms with a value of US$500 a carat or higher. Page 26.

As the gold industry suffers following the decision by the Reserve Bank to sell off most of its gold reserves, small players in the exciting Gawler Craton region are seeking joint venture partners to ensure their survival. In addition, Macraes Mining will defer any expansion of its mine north of Dunedin in New Zealand. Page 27.

The Federal Court was yesterday told by Canadian broadcaster CanWest's chief executive Izzy Asper that the company believed it had the right, if it wanted, to replace the directors of Selli and Donholken, which collectively bought 19 per cent of Network Tn with CanWest funding. Page 27.

Smart card manufacturer and processor Leigh-Mardon says the use of electronic funds transfer systems by consumers will double to about A$500 million within two years due to the onset of smart card technology. Leigh-Mardon expects to launch millions of smart cards into the consumer market at the beginning of 1998. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Melbourne-based stockbroker JB Were & Son faces a A$25,000 fine and the loss of its securities licence after being forced to admit it breached the Corporations Law while handling the sale of a 40 per cent stake in magazine group PMP Communications . The beach may place its role as the global co-ordinator for the Telstra float in jeopardy. Page 25.

Following a jump of 38 per cent in Australis Media shares yesterday, the Australian Stock Exchange suspended shares in the satellite pay TV operator as stockbroker SBC Warburg hoped to find 4.8 per cent for a corporate buyer. The buying came as Australis prepared to announce a merger with its rival Foxtel. Page 25.

Acrimonious debate over administrative matters and questions of promotion, has seen law firm Allen Allen and Hemsley's litigation department split into two units, with half the partners remaining on the 18th floor, and the other half moving to the 21st flor. Managing partner Stephen Walker said the split was due to strong growth in the firm. Page 25.

After giving evidence to the Federal Court yesterday CanWest Global Communications head Izzy Asper said he does not know how the company will cut its shareholding in Ten Group, before the impending September 30 deadline to do so. Asper said the company was exploring up to four options. Page 25.

Despite fears it may not play a part in the deal, National Mutual is confident it will have an equity stake in an expansion by its French parent Axa-UAP into China. Managing director Geoff Tomlinson said Axa-UAP would face problems under Australia's Foregn Acquisitions and Takeovers Act if it did not include National Mutual in the deal. Page 27.

Rothschild Australia Asset Management, which holds 15.6 per cent of Hawker Richardson, has criticised Austrim's takeover offer of Hawker, saying it did not reflect the true value of the group. The claim has increased pressure on Austrim to increase the bd above the current A$1.86 a share. Page 27.
THE AGE

Melbourne's establishment stockbroking house JB Were & Son has agreed to a independent review of all its internal compliance procedures, and cannot vote its 10.25 per cent stake in PMP Communications after admitting to the Australian Securities Commission that it breached the Corporations Law in the A$325 million share distribution of PMP. Page B1.

Australia's All Ordinaries Index jumped 37.2 points in morning trade yesterday, closing 23.3 points up at 2669.7 following the performance of the New York Stock Exchange's leading index, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which surged past the 8000 mark fo the first time. Page B1.

The Australian Stock Exchange suspended the trading of Australis Media shares and queried a frenzied jump in shares just minutes before the stockmarket closed yesterday. The suspension came as merger negotiations continued between Australis and News Corpration joint venture Foxtel. Page B1.

It is believed the National Australia Bank has pulled the plug on its proposed A$2.4 billion-plus takeover of United States credit card issuer Advanta Corporation, which may have become too expensive following the announcement of its US$5.4 million second quarter profit. Page B3.

Despite a strong comeback from rival brewer Lion Nathan, Carlton & United Breweries chief operating officer Nun D'Aquino said yesterday the brewer has lifted its share of the Australian beer market to more than 55 per cent in the twelve months to June. Page B3.

Several business leaders, including Australian Chamber of Manufacturers national chief executive Allan Handberg, yesterday said the Federal Government's move towards an interventionist industry policy showed it acknowledges the "real world" workings of the global economy. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
